title: Math · Kindergarten
description: An original starter path: build the idea, work an example, then try it. A focused introduction, ready to grow with your class.
framework: Original introductory mathematics practice; suggested grade placement, not a complete standards syllabus.
sequenceNote: Suggested teaching sequence, not mandated unit order.
alignmentNote: Starter course; not full grade-level coverage.

lessons.title: Count once
lessons.reading: Match one number to each object. The last number says how many are in the whole group. Moving the objects does not change the total.
lessons.easyReading: Match one number to each object. The last number says how many are in the whole group. Moving the objects does not change the total.
lessons.expertReading: Match one number to each object. The last number says how many are in the whole group. Moving the objects does not change the total. A rearrangement preserves the number of objects when none are added or removed.
lessons.worked: Touch four blocks: 1, 2, 3, 4. There are four blocks.

application.prompt: You count seven buttons, touching each once. How many buttons are there?
application.explanation: 7. Match one number to each object. The last number says how many are in the whole group. Moving the objects does not change the total.

vocab.definition: Find the size of a group by matching one number to each object.

lessons.practice: Explain how count helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 7. Match one number to each object. The last number says how many are in the whole group. Moving the objects does not change the total.

lessons.title: Nothing is a number
lessons.reading: Zero tells us that a group has no objects. It is different from one. An empty basket still has a quantity we can describe.
lessons.easyReading: Zero tells us that a group has no objects. It is different from one. An empty basket still has a quantity we can describe.
lessons.expertReading: Zero tells us that a group has no objects. It is different from one. An empty basket still has a quantity we can describe. Zero is the starting point when counting how many objects are present.
lessons.worked: A basket held two apples. Both were removed, so zero apples remain.
steps: Both were removed, so zero apples remain.

application.prompt: A plate has no crackers. Which number describes it?
application.explanation: 0. Zero tells us that a group has no objects. It is different from one. An empty basket still has a quantity we can describe.

vocab.definition: The number that describes an empty group.

lessons.practice: Explain how zero helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 0. Zero tells us that a group has no objects. It is different from one. An empty basket still has a quantity we can describe.

lessons.title: Compare two groups
lessons.reading: A group has more when it has objects left after matching one to one with another group. Count both groups to check.
lessons.easyReading: A group has more when it has objects left after matching one to one with another group. Count both groups to check.
lessons.expertReading: A group has more when it has objects left after matching one to one with another group. Count both groups to check. One-to-one matching compares quantities without relying on how spread out the objects look.
lessons.worked: Match five red blocks with three blue blocks. Two red blocks remain unmatched, so five is greater.
steps: Match five red blocks with three blue blocks
Two red blocks remain unmatched, so five is greater.

application.explanation: 6 shells. A group has more when it has objects left after matching one to one with another group. Count both groups to check.

lessons.practice: Explain how greater than helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 6 shells. A group has more when it has objects left after matching one to one with another group. Count both groups to check.

lessons.title: Join groups
lessons.reading: Addition joins quantities. Count the first group, then keep counting as objects from the second group are included.
lessons.easyReading: Addition joins quantities. Count the first group, then keep counting as objects from the second group are included.
lessons.expertReading: Addition joins quantities. Count the first group, then keep counting as objects from the second group are included. The same total can be composed from different pairs of smaller quantities.
lessons.worked: Three cubes and two more make five: 3 + 2 = 5.
steps: Three cubes and two more make five: 3 + 2 = 5.

application.prompt: Four birds are joined by two birds. How many birds are there?
application.explanation: 6. Addition joins quantities. Count the first group, then keep counting as objects from the second group are included.

vocab.definition: Combining quantities to find a total.

lessons.practice: Explain how addition helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 6. Addition joins quantities. Count the first group, then keep counting as objects from the second group are included.

lessons.title: Name a shape
lessons.reading: Look at a shape’s straight sides and corners. A triangle has three straight sides. Turning a shape does not change its name.
lessons.easyReading: Look at a shape’s straight sides and corners. A triangle has three straight sides. Turning a shape does not change its name.
lessons.expertReading: Look at a shape’s straight sides and corners. A triangle has three straight sides. Turning a shape does not change its name. Shape categories depend on defining properties, not orientation or size.
lessons.worked: A shape with three straight sides meeting at three corners is a triangle, even when one corner points down.
steps: A shape with three straight sides meeting at three corners is a triangle, even when one corner points down.

application.prompt: Which shape has three straight sides?
application.explanation: Triangle. Look at a shape’s straight sides and corners. A triangle has three straight sides. Turning a shape does not change its name.

vocab.definition: A closed flat shape with three straight sides.

lessons.practice: Explain how triangle helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: Triangle. Look at a shape’s straight sides and corners. A triangle has three straight sides. Turning a shape does not change its name.
